sources.title: Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next · Hugging Face
sources.snippet: Today, we are sharing a concrete step in that direction: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. This experimental preview of the architecture that will underpin Qwen4 is built around a fundamental rethinking of how the core components of modern large language models (LLMs) interact at scale.

sources.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next for Local AI in 2026: 180B on Disk, 6B Active, and ...
sources.snippet: TL;DR: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (released August 26, 2026) is a 180B-parameter MoE with only 6B active per token — and 51B of those parameters are an n-gram lookup table that can stream from your NVMe drive instead of sitting in RAM.

sources.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next - GitHub
sources.snippet: Compared with Qwen3.7-Plus, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next substantially reduces both training and inference cost — training takes only about 1/9 as much, yet it delivers superior capabilities in coding and office tasks.

sources.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on Windows (Strix Halo) - GitHub
sources.snippet: This repo is the Windows build, deployment, and serving layer around that work. No binaries, no weights. You build the engine from source and pull the GGUFs from unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF.

sources.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-StrixHalo-Verified - Hugging Face
sources.snippet: I'm looking for a role in LLM inference and applied AI (local and on-prem inference, performance engineering, model evaluation), remote or around Pau, France. This runtime is a side project; I'm a physiotherapist by training — more about me at the end of this card.
